prompt.adult: When the LORD began to speak by Hosea, He told him to take a wife. Whom did Hosea take?
prompt.child: God gave the prophet Hosea an unusual message about his own family. Whom did Hosea marry?
prompt.teen: Hosea 1:3 says, “So he went and took” someone, who bore him a son. Whom did Hosea take as his wife?
prompt.older: According to Hosea 1:3, whom did Hosea take as his wife?

verses.text: So he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.

explanation.adult: Look at the start of 1:3, right after “So he went and took.”
explanation.child: Read the beginning of verse 3. The name comes right after “took.”
explanation.teen: 1:3 opens with Hosea obeying. The name and family follow “So he went and took.”
explanation.older: The name follows “So he went and took” at the opening of 1:3.

teaching.extended_explanation: Hosea prophesied in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah of Judah and Jeroboam of Israel (1:1). The LORD made Hosea’s own marriage a picture of Israel’s unfaithfulness and of His faithful love. 1:3 opens by naming the woman Hosea took, and says she bore him a son.
teaching.takeaway: Hosea took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim as his wife.

prompt.adult: The LORD remembers loving Israel when Israel was a child. From where does He say He called His son?
prompt.child: God says He loved Israel when Israel was a child. Where did God call His son out of?
prompt.teen: Hosea 11:1 opens with God’s love for Israel as a child. What does the second line say God did?
prompt.older: According to Hosea 11:1, from where did God call His son?

verses.text: “When Israel was a child, I loved him, And out of Egypt I called My son.

explanation.adult: Read the second line of 11:1, right before “I called My son.”
explanation.child: Look at the end of verse 1. The place is named just before “I called My son.”
explanation.teen: 11:1 has two lines. The place begins the second one, ahead of “I called My son.”
explanation.older: The second line of 11:1 names it, before “I called My son.”

teaching.extended_explanation: Hosea 11 is a tender poem about God as a father. 11:1 looks back to Israel’s beginnings as a people, when God loved Israel as a child, and names the place from which He called His son. 11:2 then tells how, the more they were called, the more they went after the Baals.
teaching.takeaway: God says, “out of Egypt I called My son.”

prompt.adult: The LORD says He will allure her, bring her into the wilderness, speak comfort to her, and give her vineyards. What will the Valley of Achor become?
prompt.child: God says He will lead His people into the wilderness and speak kindly to them. A valley called Achor will become something new. What?
prompt.teen: In Hosea 2:15, God gives her vineyards and “the Valley of Achor as” what?
prompt.older: According to Hosea 2:15, what will the Valley of Achor be?

verses.text: “Therefore, behold, I will allure her, Will bring her into the wilderness, And speak comfort to her.
I will give her her vineyards from there, And the Valley of Achor as a door of hope; She shall sing there, As in the days of her youth, As in the day when she came up from the land of Egypt.

explanation.adult: Read 2:15 right after “the Valley of Achor as.”
explanation.child: In verse 15, find “the Valley of Achor as.” The words come right after it.
explanation.teen: 2:15 gives two gifts. The second is the valley, followed by what it will be after “as.”
explanation.older: It follows “the Valley of Achor as” in the first sentence of 2:15.

teaching.extended_explanation: After the judgments of 2:2-13, the LORD’s tone changes with “Therefore, behold” (2:14). He will lead her into the wilderness and speak comfort, give her vineyards, and turn the Valley of Achor, remembered as a place of trouble since Joshua 7, into something new. She will sing there as in the days of her youth.
teaching.takeaway: God will give “the Valley of Achor as a door of hope.”

prompt.adult: “In that day,” says the LORD, she will call Him “My Husband.” What will she no longer call Him?
prompt.child: God says a day will come when His people will call Him “My Husband.” What name will they stop using for Him?
prompt.teen: In Hosea 2:16, the LORD says, “you will call Me ‘My Husband,’ And no longer call Me” what?
prompt.older: According to Hosea 2:16, what will she no longer call the LORD?

verses.text: “And it shall be, in that day,” Says the LORD, “That you will call Me ‘My Husband,’ And no longer call Me ‘My Master,’
For I will take from her mouth the names of the Baals, And they shall be remembered by their name no more.

explanation.adult: Read the end of 2:16, after “And no longer call Me.”
explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 16. The name comes after “no longer call Me.”
explanation.teen: 2:16 sets two names against each other. The second follows “no longer call Me.”
explanation.older: The name that closes 2:16 follows “And no longer call Me.”

teaching.extended_explanation: In 2:16-17 the LORD promises a new relationship. 2:16 contrasts two names she might use for Him, one she will use and one she will drop. 2:17 explains that He will take the names of the Baals from her mouth.
teaching.takeaway: She will call Him “My Husband,” and no longer “My Master.”

prompt.adult: God says He taught Ephraim to walk, taking them by their arms (11:3). He drew them with gentle cords, and with what else?
prompt.child: God says He taught Ephraim to walk like a small child, holding their arms. He says He drew them with gentle cords and with what else?
prompt.teen: In Hosea 11:4, “I drew them with gentle cords,” and what follows?
prompt.older: According to Hosea 11:4, with what did God draw them, along with gentle cords?

verses.text: “I taught Ephraim to walk, Taking them by their arms; But they did not know that I healed them.
I drew them with gentle cords, With bands of love, And I was to them as those who take the yoke from their neck. I stooped and fed them.

explanation.adult: Read the second line of 11:4, right after “gentle cords.”
explanation.child: Look at verse 4. The words come right after “I drew them with gentle cords.”
explanation.teen: 11:4 opens with two parallel lines. Read the second.
explanation.older: The second line of 11:4, after “gentle cords,” gives it.

teaching.extended_explanation: 11:3-4 pictures God as a parent: teaching Ephraim to walk, taking them by their arms, healing them, and stooping to feed them. 11:4 opens with two parallel lines about how He drew them, then speaks of taking the yoke from their neck. Read the second line.
teaching.takeaway: “I drew them with gentle cords, With bands of love.”

prompt.adult: Hosea’s son was named Lo-Ammi, “For you are not My people” (1:9). In 2:23 God says to those who were not His people, “You are My people!” How do they reply?
prompt.child: Hosea named his son Lo-Ammi, which means “not My people.” Later God promises to say, “You are My people!” What will the people say back?
prompt.teen: Connect Hosea 1:9 and 2:23. After God says, “You are My people!” what do they say in reply?
prompt.older: According to Hosea 2:23, what will they say when God calls them His people?

verses.text: Then God said: “Call his name Lo-Ammi, For you are not My people, And I will not be your God.

Then I will sow her for Myself in the earth, And I will have mercy on her who had not obtained mercy; Then I will say to those who were not My people, ‘You are My people!’ And they shall say, ‘You are my God!’ ”

explanation.adult: Read the final quotation of 2:23, after “And they shall say.”
explanation.child: Look at the very end of verse 23. Their reply comes after “they shall say.”
explanation.teen: 2:23 ends with an exchange. Read the second quotation, after “they shall say.”
explanation.older: The closing quotation of 2:23 follows “And they shall say.”

teaching.extended_explanation: In 1:9 God names Hosea’s third child Lo-Ammi with the words “For you are not My people.” 2:23 reverses the names: mercy for her who had not obtained mercy, and “You are My people!” to those who were not His people. Their reply closes the verse.
teaching.takeaway: God will say, “You are My people!” and they shall say, “You are my God!”

prompt.adult: God cries out, “How can I give you up, Ephraim?” (11:8). In the closing chapter, after Israel returns, what does God say Ephraim shall say (14:8)?
prompt.child: God says, “How can I give you up, Ephraim?” because He loves His people so much. At the end of the book, what does God say Ephraim will say?
prompt.teen: Connect Hosea 11:8 and 14:8. In 14:8, “Ephraim shall say” what?
prompt.older: According to Hosea 14:8, what shall Ephraim say?

choices.text: Why have You forsaken Your people?
Where are the idols we served before?
What have I to do anymore with idols?
When will the LORD return to Zion again?

verses.text: “How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel? How can I make you like Admah? How can I set you like Zeboiim? My heart churns within Me; My sympathy is stirred.
“Ephraim shall say, ‘What have I to do anymore with idols?’ I have heard and observed him. I am like a green cypress tree; Your fruit is found in Me.”

explanation.adult: Read the quotation at the start of 14:8, after “Ephraim shall say.”
explanation.child: Look at the beginning of verse 14:8. Ephraim’s words come right after “Ephraim shall say.”
explanation.teen: 14:8 opens with Ephraim’s quoted words. Read them after “shall say.”
explanation.older: The quotation that opens 14:8 follows “Ephraim shall say.”

teaching.extended_explanation: In 11:8-9 God’s heart churns within Him; He will not give Ephraim up or destroy him, for He is God and not man. Chapter 14 calls Israel to return with words (14:1-3), and God promises healing and love. 14:8 opens with what Ephraim shall say, then God answers, “I have heard and observed him.”
teaching.takeaway: Ephraim shall say, “What have I to do anymore with idols?”

prompt.adult: Hosea calls, “O Israel, return to the LORD your God” (14:1). In 3:5, whom does he say the children of Israel shall seek in the latter days, along with the LORD their God?
prompt.child: Hosea begs Israel to return to the LORD. Earlier he said that one day Israel would return and seek the LORD their God and someone else. Who?
prompt.teen: Connect Hosea 3:5 and 14:1. In 3:5, Israel shall “return and seek the LORD their God and” whom?
prompt.older: According to Hosea 3:5, whom shall the children of Israel seek along with the LORD their God?

verses.text: Afterward the children of Israel shall return and seek the LORD their God and David their king. They shall fear the LORD and His goodness in the latter days.
O Israel, return to the LORD your God, For you have stumbled because of your iniquity;

explanation.adult: Read 3:5 right after “seek the LORD their God and.”
explanation.child: In verse 3:5, find “the LORD their God and.” The person comes right after.
explanation.teen: 3:5 names two whom Israel shall seek. The second follows “and.”
explanation.older: The second one sought in 3:5 follows “the LORD their God and.”

teaching.extended_explanation: 3:4 says Israel will live many days without king, prince, sacrifice, or sacred pillar. 3:5 looks past that to the latter days, when they will return and seek the LORD their God and one more, and fear the LORD and His goodness. 14:1-2 gives the call to return, with words of repentance.
teaching.takeaway: In the latter days Israel shall seek the LORD their God and David their king.
